passage:
Dear Rehana,
You know the creator I keep going on about? Yesterday he posted that his "secret trading course" was closing in two hours and only fifty seats remained. Everyone in the comments wrote "joined, life changed". I had Dad's payment app open on the family tablet and my thumb was actually on the button.
Then I remembered what you said about checking who profits. I looked: the same profile was also pushing a betting app, and the comments all sounded alike. I closed the app. That money isn't mine anyway, it's for the rent and Dad's shop.
I told Dad what I nearly did. He wasn't angry, just quiet for a while, and then he thanked me.
Write back soon.
Jyoti

qa.q: What did Jyoti find on the creator's profile besides the course?
qa.a: The same profile was also pushing a betting app.

qa.q: How did Jyoti feel on closing the app, and why?
qa.a: Jyoti had grown suspicious after checking who profits and seeing the alike comments, and realised the money for the rent and Dad's shop was not Jyoti's to spend.

qa.q: What could Jyoti do if the creator posts another countdown offer?
qa.a: Jyoti can treat the countdown as pressure, check the claims, ask a trusted adult before anything involving money, and never spend money that belongs to someone else.

qa.q: How might Jyoti's dad have felt on hearing what Jyoti nearly did?
qa.a: His quiet suggests worry, and his thanks suggest he was relieved and grateful that Jyoti told him.

grounding: Shows a teen recognising a creator monetising fans' trust and stopping before spending money that is not hers.

passage:
It was exam week, and Simran had almost no pocket money left. But the video made it sound so simple.

The creator, who had helped her with physics for a year through free videos, was launching a "Topper Guarantee" course. "Only 5,999 today! Rank guaranteed or your money back!" A timer counted down. Forty-seven minutes.

Simran knew her mother's card was saved on the laptop. Her fingers hovered.

Her elder sister Seema walked in with two cups of tea. "What's that?" Simran explained, fast.

Seema read the page slowly. "Guaranteed rank? Nobody can guarantee that. And look at the refund terms." They were tiny: refund only if you "complete all modules and attend all live sessions," which was impossible during exams.

"But he's been so helpful," Simran said. "I trust him."

"That's what he's selling," Seema said gently. "Your trust. And it's Mummy's money, not yours."

Simran closed the laptop. The timer was still running. She let it.

qa.q: How long was left on the countdown timer?
qa.a: Forty-seven minutes were left on the timer.

qa.q: What was Simran feeling as her fingers hovered over the card?
qa.a: Simran felt tempted and pressured, trusting the creator and anxious about exams.

qa.q: What did Seema help Simran notice?
qa.a: Seema pointed out that no one can guarantee a rank, the refund terms were nearly impossible, and the money belonged to their mother.

qa.q: How might their mother have felt if the card had been used?
qa.a: Their mother would likely have felt upset and worried, both about the money and about how easily trust had been used to sell to Simran.

grounding: It shows a teen targeted by a creator who sells an expensive course to young fans, recognising that trust built online can be sold, checking claims and not spending money that is not hers.

passage:
In the back of the school bus in Thane, Chetan held out his phone to Eshaan. "Look at this. That gaming creator we watch. He says this app doubled his money in a day. You just predict match results."

Eshaan watched. The creator was laughing, a pile of notes on his desk. At the bottom, in small letters: "promotional content."

"It's betting," Eshaan said. "He's getting paid to show that."

Chetan went quiet. Then, "I already tried. I put in the money Papa gave me for the tuition fee. I lost it. Two thousand." His voice cracked. "I thought I'd win it back. Now it's all gone, and I'm scared to tell him."

Eshaan felt his own chest go tight. "You have to tell someone today. I'll come with you."

After school they went to Chetan's flat. Chetan's father listened, very serious, then put his hand on his son's shoulder. "I'm glad you told me. We'll delete this app together tonight and talk to your tuition sir about the fee."

qa.q: What did the small letters at the bottom of the video say?
What was Chetan feeling when he admitted losing the tuition money?
qa.a: Chetan felt scared and ashamed, his voice cracking, because he had lost the money and feared telling his father.

qa.q: What did Eshaan do that was wise?
qa.a: Eshaan named the app as betting, noticed the video was paid promotion, and went with Chetan to tell his father that same day.

qa.q: How did Chetan's father respond, and why did it help?
qa.a: He stayed calm, said he was glad Chetan told him and planned to delete the app and talk to the tuition teacher, which made Chetan feel supported instead of punished.

grounding: It shows teens recognising that a trusted creator is promoting a betting app to young fans, and a friend's loss being taken to a trusted adult the same day.
